items.title: Microsoft Entra ID Introduces Continuous Access Evaluation for High-Risk Sessions
items.summary: Microsoft has expanded Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) to cover high-risk sign-in sessions, enabling near real-time policy enforcement. The update allows organisations to revoke access tokens within seconds of detecting anomalous behaviour, closing the window attackers exploit between token issuance and expiry.

items.title: SailPoint Unveils Atlas AI: Autonomous Identity Governance That Writes Its Own Policies
items.summary: SailPoint has launched Atlas AI, an autonomous identity governance engine that analyses entitlements across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem systems and auto-generates access policies without manual rule creation. The system can certify 80% of access reviews automatically and escalates anomalous entitlements for human review, cutting certification cycles from weeks to hours.

items.title: CyberArk Extends Privileged Access Controls to AI Agents and LLM Workloads
items.summary: CyberArk has announced native support for securing AI agent identities, extending its Privileged Access Manager to govern LLM-based workloads accessing sensitive enterprise systems. The solution issues short-lived credentials to AI agents, enforces least-privilege access policies per workflow step, and maintains a full audit trail of AI-initiated actions for compliance purposes.

items.title: BeyondTrust Patches Critical Remote Code Execution Flaw in Privileged Remote Access
items.summary: BeyondTrust has released an emergency patch for CVE-2026-31892, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in its Privileged Remote Access (PRA) product rated CVSS 9.8. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on PRA appliances. CISA has added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and federal agencies must patch within 48 hours.

items.title: Passkey Adoption Surges Past 1 Billion Accounts as Enterprises Retire SMS OTP
items.summary: The FIDO Alliance reports passkey adoption has crossed 1 billion accounts globally, driven by expanded platform support from Google and Apple. Enterprises are rapidly deploying passkeys as a replacement for SMS OTP, with phishing resistance and reduced helpdesk load cited as primary motivators.

items.title: Veza Raises $108M Series D to Scale Identity Security Graph Platform
items.summary: Veza, the identity security company built around a graph-based authorisation model, has raised $108M in Series D funding led by Accel. The platform maps human and machine identities to the data and systems they can access across cloud, SaaS, and data infrastructure. The funding will accelerate its non-human identity and AI workload governance capabilities.

items.title: Opal Security Launches AI Access Governance to Control What AI Agents Can Do
items.summary: Opal Security has introduced AI Access Governance, a module that applies just-in-time access controls and approval workflows to AI agent actions. When an AI agent requests access to a sensitive resource — a database, API, or internal tool — Opal intercepts the request, validates it against policy, and routes high-risk requests for human approval in real time.

items.title: Permiso Detects Identity-Based Attacks Across Cloud Environments Using Behavioural AI
items.summary: Permiso has expanded its cloud identity threat detection platform with a new behavioural AI engine that establishes per-identity baselines across AWS, Azure, GCP, and SaaS applications. The engine flags lateral movement, unusual API call sequences, and privilege escalation attempts by both human and non-human identities, reducing mean time to detect identity-based attacks by 73%.

items.title: Aembit Launches Workload IAM Platform to Secure Machine-to-Machine Access
items.summary: Aembit has launched a workload identity and access management platform designed for machine-to-machine communication in modern cloud-native environments. The platform issues short-lived, cryptographically attested credentials to workloads using SPIFFE-compatible identity documents, eliminating static API keys and secrets from CI/CD pipelines and service meshes.

items.title: Delinea Adds AI-Powered Privilege Anomaly Detection to Secret Server
items.summary: Delinea has added an AI-powered anomaly detection engine to Secret Server that monitors privileged session behaviour and flags deviations from established baselines in real time. The update also introduces automated secret rotation for DevOps pipelines and extends PAM controls to Kubernetes workloads, addressing the growing challenge of ephemeral infrastructure credentials.

items.title: Saviynt Expands CPAM to Cover Non-Human Identities and AI Service Accounts
items.summary: Saviynt has expanded its Cloud Privileged Access Management (CPAM) module to govern non-human identities including AI service accounts, CI/CD pipeline identities, and cloud function execution roles. The platform now provides full lifecycle management, access certification, and anomaly detection for machine identities, which Saviynt reports now outnumber human identities 40:1 in its customer base.

items.title: The State of Identity Security 2026 — IDSA & CrowdStrike Annual Report
items.summary: The Identity Defined Security Alliance's annual survey of 500 security leaders finds 84% of organisations suffered an identity-related breach in the past year. Non-human accounts now outnumber human accounts 45:1 in the average enterprise. AI agent identities are identified as the fastest-growing unmanaged attack surface, with 71% of respondents lacking visibility into what AI workloads can access.

items.title: Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management 2026
items.summary: Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Access Management evaluates 16 vendors. Microsoft, Okta, and Ping Identity lead as Leaders. The report notes a market shift toward identity fabric architectures and AI-native policy engines. Vendors lacking non-human identity management are increasingly penalised in evaluation criteria as machine identities dominate enterprise environments.

items.title: Forrester Wave: Privileged Identity Management Q2 2026
items.summary: Forrester's Q2 2026 Wave for Privileged Identity Management evaluates CyberArk, BeyondTrust, Delinea, and seven others. The report identifies cloud-native PAM and secrets management for AI/DevOps pipelines as the fastest-growing evaluation criteria. Non-human identity lifecycle management is now a mandatory capability for Leader classification.

items.title: NIST SP 800-207A: Zero Trust Architecture for Multi-Cloud — Public Draft
items.summary: NIST has published a draft of SP 800-207A extending Zero Trust Architecture guidance to multi-cloud and hybrid deployments. The draft introduces a cloud-agnostic policy decision point model and provides reference architectures for identity-centric zero trust across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Public comment period closes July 15, 2026.

items.title: SANS 2026 IAM Survey: 61% Lack Visibility into Privileged Accounts Across Hybrid Environments
items.summary: The SANS Institute's annual IAM survey of 1,200 practitioners reveals 61% lack full visibility into privileged accounts across hybrid environments. Credential-based attacks remain the top initial access vector for the fourth consecutive year. Only 38% have implemented JIT access. AI agent identities are now cited as the top emerging blind spot.

items.title: North Korean Lazarus Group Exploits SAML Assertion Forgery in Enterprise SSO Attack
items.summary: Security researchers have attributed a sophisticated supply chain attack to Lazarus Group, leveraging SAML assertion forgery to pivot from a compromised IdP into downstream SaaS applications. The attack bypassed MFA by hijacking federated sessions post-authentication, affecting 40 enterprise customers of a major SSO provider.

items.title: Scattered Spider Returns: AI Voice Deepfakes Used to Reset MFA at Fortune 500 Help Desks
items.summary: Scattered Spider has resumed targeting enterprise identity provider help desks using AI-generated voice deepfakes to bypass identity verification and trigger MFA resets. At least six Fortune 500 companies were targeted in May 2026. Security teams are advised to implement callback verification with out-of-band authentication for all identity resets.

items.title: EU eIDAS 2.0 Digital Identity Wallet: Implementation Deadline Looms for Member States
items.summary: European Union member states face a Q4 2026 deadline to begin rollout of eIDAS 2.0-compliant digital identity wallets. The regulation mandates citizens can use government-issued digital identities for online public and private sector services. Industry groups warn interoperability between national wallet implementations remains a significant unsolved challenge.

items.title: Healthcare Giant Medaura Confirms 2.1M Patient Records Exposed via Stolen VPN Credentials
items.summary: Medaura Health confirmed a breach affecting 2.1 million patient records after attackers used stolen VPN credentials from a third-party contractor. The absence of MFA on the contractor portal enabled initial access. Attackers maintained persistence for 47 days before detection, exfiltrating names, SSNs, insurance records, and clinical notes.

items.title: Financial Firm Loses $18M After Credential Stuffing Attack Bypasses SMS MFA via SIM Swap
items.summary: A regional US bank disclosed 34,000 customer accounts compromised through a credential stuffing attack using credentials from third-party breaches. Attackers bypassed SMS MFA by performing SIM swaps on high-value accounts, resulting in $18M in fraudulent transfers. The bank is migrating to hardware token and passkey authentication.

items.title: Cloud Provider Breach: Over-Privileged Service Account Exposes Data of 60 Enterprise Tenants
items.summary: A cloud infrastructure provider disclosed that a threat actor compromised an over-privileged service account with cross-tenant administrative rights, gaining access to data belonging to 60 enterprise customers. The service account lacked rotation policies and had not been audited in 18 months. CISA is investigating.

items.title: Telecom Carrier Breach: 800K Identity Records Exposed After SSO Token Theft
items.summary: A major telecom carrier reported a breach of 800,000 employee and contractor identity records after attackers stole long-lived SSO session tokens from an unpatched identity provider instance. Tokens were used to access HR systems, payroll data, and internal wikis without triggering authentication alerts.

items.title: Retailer Confirms 1.4M Card Records Stolen After Phishing Compromised AD Admin Account
items.summary: A national retail chain confirmed a point-of-sale breach affecting 1.4 million payment card records, traced to a phishing attack on a help desk agent with broad Active Directory administrative rights. The attacker used the compromised account to deploy credential-harvesting malware across 300 store systems.
